Database activity monitoring feeding a separate log store
Daily snapshots of the database
questions.explanation: Independent monitoring of queries records and can alert on privileged abuse. Volume encryption does not stop an authorized session reading data, passwords do not log activity and snapshots capture state, not reads.

questions.question: Which TWO activities belong to the earliest phases of the cloud data life cycle? (Choose two.)
options: Legal hold release
Moving to long-term archival storage
Classifying the data when it is created
Verified destruction of media
Assigning an owner and applying initial labels
questions.explanation: Classification and ownership are applied when data is created. Destruction, archiving and hold release occur later in the cycle.

questions.question: Which TWO measures MOST effectively reduce the risk of public exposure of cloud object storage? (Choose two.)
options: Disabling versioning on every bucket
Account-level controls that block public access by default
Naming buckets with hard-to-guess names
Relying on the bucket's default network location
Continuous posture monitoring that alerts on public or unencrypted buckets
questions.explanation: Preventive guardrails and detective posture monitoring address misconfiguration. Obscure names are security by obscurity, defaults are the common cause of exposure and versioning is a recovery feature unrelated to exposure.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about data classification are correct? (Choose two.)
options: Handling rules such as encryption and access follow from the label
It applies only to structured data
It is assigned by the cloud provider after migration
It is unnecessary if data is encrypted
It must be reviewed because sensitivity can change over time
questions.explanation: Labels drive controls and need periodic review. Providers do not decide the owner's classification, encryption does not replace classification and it applies to all data types.

questions.question: Deleting a file in the cloud console guarantees that every replica of the underlying data has been physically destroyed.
questions.explanation: Logical deletion does not guarantee physical erasure; customers rely on cryptographic erasure and provider attestations.

questions.question: Data discovery should generally take place before classification and DLP rules are tuned.
questions.explanation: You must know where data is and what it contains before labeling it or writing effective prevention rules.

questions.question: Anonymized data that cannot reasonably be re-identified is generally outside the scope of privacy regulations such as GDPR.
questions.explanation: Properly anonymized data no longer relates to an identifiable person, unlike pseudonymized data.

questions.question: Information rights management can restrict printing and forwarding of a document after it has been shared.
questions.explanation: IRM policies are embedded and enforced when the document is opened, and access can be revoked.

questions.question: A cloud customer can transfer accountability for data protection to the provider by signing a processor contract.
questions.explanation: A contract assigns processing duties, but the controller stays accountable to regulators and data subjects.

questions.question: Static data masking creates a copy with realistic substitute values that cannot be reversed to the original.
questions.explanation: Static masking is typically irreversible and suits non-production copies.

questions.question: A regulator requires that the cloud provider must never be able to decrypt a firm's trading records. Which key strategy BEST satisfies this requirement?
options: Provider-managed keys held in the provider's HSM
Provider-managed keys held in the provider's HSM with rotation every 90 days
Bring your own key imported into the provider's KMS
Hold your own key in an on-premises HSM outside the provider's control
questions.explanation: HYOK keeps key material outside the provider so it cannot decrypt. BYOK still imports the key where the provider's service can use it, and provider-managed keys, however rotated or hardened, are provider-accessible.
questions.whyTested: BYOK versus HYOK is a favorite judgement question.

questions.question: A company wants to retain the ability to revoke access to data at any time by deleting key material, but accepts that the provider's service performs encryption and decryption. Which option fits?
options: Hashing the data with a salted algorithm
Customer-managed keys in the provider's key service, with customer-controlled policies
Provider-managed keys with default settings
Storing the key beside the encrypted data in the same account to make recovery easier
questions.explanation: Customer-managed keys let the customer disable or delete the key and so cut off access. Defaults leave control to the provider, hashing is irreversible and cannot protect data that must be read, and co-locating the key with data undermines separation.

questions.question: In envelope encryption, what is the main advantage of wrapping each data encryption key with a key encryption key?
options: Rotating or revoking one key encryption key controls many data keys without re-encrypting data
It removes the need for any key management service
It makes the encryption algorithm quantum resistant
It lets the provider decrypt the data on demand without needing any customer approval or key policy check
questions.explanation: The KEK protects DEKs, so rotation and revocation happen at the KEK level. Envelope encryption still needs key management, does not change algorithm strength and does not give the provider extra decryption rights.

questions.question: An e-commerce site wants to shrink the part of its environment that must meet card-data compliance rules. Which technique MOST directly achieves this?
options: Tokenization so most systems only hold surrogate values
Encrypting card numbers with a key stored in the application
Compressing card numbers before storing them
Hashing card numbers with an unsalted algorithm
questions.explanation: Systems that hold only tokens are generally out of scope for the real value, shrinking compliance effort. Unsalted hashes of low-entropy numbers are easily reversed, compression is not security and an application-held key leaves the data in scope.

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes tokenization from encryption?
options: A token is created by applying a block cipher and a secret key to the original value
A token can be reversed by anyone holding the public key
A token has no mathematical relationship to the value, which sits in a vault
A token is always shorter than the original value
questions.explanation: Tokens are random surrogates mapped in a vault, so there is nothing to decrypt. Reversal by public key, size and cipher-based creation describe encryption or format-preserving encryption instead.

questions.question: A team stores API keys for a payment service in the configuration file of a container image. What is the BEST remediation?
options: Encrypt the configuration file using a hard-coded password
Move the keys into a secrets manager and inject them at runtime with rotation enabled
Rename the keys so they are harder to recognize
Restrict the container registry to internal users only
questions.explanation: A secrets manager provides access control, audit and rotation, and keeps secrets out of images. A hard-coded password just moves the secret, registry restrictions do not remove embedded secrets and renaming is obscurity.

questions.question: Which situation BEST justifies using a hardware security module rather than software-only key storage?
options: The team wants to avoid learning key management
A policy requires tamper-resistant, validated protection of root keys
The application needs much faster bulk encryption of large video files at low cost
The data is classified as public
questions.explanation: HSMs provide tamper-resistant custody and validated modules for sensitive keys. They are not for speeding bulk encryption, do not eliminate key management duties and public data does not justify the cost.

questions.question: Two parties who have never met need to exchange a symmetric session key over an untrusted network. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Hash the key with SHA-256 and send the hash
Send the symmetric key in an email protected by a long and complex subject line
Use a pre-shared key printed on the license agreement
Use asymmetric cryptography or a key agreement protocol to establish the key
questions.explanation: Asymmetric methods or key agreement solve the key distribution problem. Email is plaintext, a hash of a key does not convey it and a printed shared secret cannot be rotated or scaled.

questions.question: An architect's design relies on encrypting data with a key kept in the same storage account as the data. What is the PRIMARY weakness?
options: The encryption algorithm will run too slowly
Anyone who gains access to the account can obtain both data and key, defeating the encryption
Keys cannot legally be stored in cloud storage
The data cannot be backed up while encrypted
questions.explanation: Key separation is a basic principle: compromise of the account should not hand over both parts. Keys can be stored in cloud services, backups work fine and performance is not the issue.

questions.question: A company discovers its TLS certificate expired and a customer-facing service went down. Which practice would MOST directly prevent a recurrence?
options: Replace TLS with a proprietary encryption protocol maintained by the application team
Automate certificate issuance and renewal and monitor expiry dates
Disable certificate validation in clients
Issue certificates with ten-year lifetimes
questions.explanation: Automation and monitoring address the lifecycle failure. Long lifetimes increase exposure when keys are compromised, disabling validation removes authentication and proprietary protocols are riskier.

questions.question: A firm must plan for the day current public-key algorithms are no longer safe. Which design principle is MOST useful?
options: Crypto agility, so algorithms can be swapped without re-architecting
Encrypting data twice with the same algorithm
Standardizing every system on the longest public-key length that is available today
Moving all keys to a single central server
questions.explanation: Agility lets teams migrate to new algorithms. Longer keys of a vulnerable family do not help against quantum attacks, double encryption with one algorithm shares the weakness and one central server is a single point of failure.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about BYOK are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: The provider can never access the key in any form
BYOK and HYOK are the same thing
The customer generates the key material and imports it into the provider's key service
The provider's service can still use the key to decrypt data on the customer's behalf
Keys are never stored outside the customer's premises
questions.explanation: BYOK improves customer control over key generation and lifecycle but the key lives in the provider's service. HYOK is the model where the key never leaves customer control.

questions.question: Which TWO controls protect data at rest in a cloud database? (Choose two.)
options: A web application firewall in front of the website
Column-level encryption of especially sensitive fields
Multi-factor authentication for console users
Transparent database or volume encryption with managed keys
TLS between the application and the database
questions.explanation: Volume or database encryption and field-level encryption protect stored data. TLS protects data in transit, a firewall protects the web layer and MFA protects authentication.

questions.question: Which TWO phases of the key lifecycle are MOST relevant to crypto-shredding? (Choose two.)
options: Archival of keys for future decryption
Destruction of the key and all of its copies
Use of one shared key across all data sets
Distribution of keys to external partners
Generation of keys that are unique to the data being protected
questions.explanation: Crypto-shredding needs per-dataset keys that can be destroyed completely. Archiving or sharing keys defeats the guarantee.

questions.question: Hashing is a reversible process that lets the original data be recovered with the right key.
questions.explanation: Hashing is one-way; encryption is the reversible operation.

questions.question: A digital signature provides integrity, origin authentication and non-repudiation.
questions.explanation: Signing a hash with the sender's private key lets anyone verify it with the public key.

questions.question: TLS protects data at rest in a cloud storage service.
questions.explanation: TLS protects data in transit; storage encryption protects data at rest.

questions.question: Rotating keys regularly limits how much data is exposed if one key is compromised.
questions.explanation: Rotation shortens key lifetime and reduces the data protected by any single key.

questions.question: Tokenization is suitable for protecting data inside a vault-backed system where real values must be retrievable by authorized services.
questions.explanation: The vault maps tokens back to real values for authorized use, while other systems never see the real data.

questions.question: Under HYOK the cloud provider can still decrypt data using keys held in its own key management service.
questions.explanation: In HYOK the keys remain outside the provider's control, so the provider cannot decrypt.

questions.question: A cloud provider hosts multiple tenants on shared hosts. Which attack is MOST directly aimed at breaking tenant isolation?
options: Cross-site scripting against a tenant's website
Brute-force guessing of a customer's console password
Virtual machine escape to the hypervisor
Phishing a customer's help desk
questions.explanation: A VM escape defeats the isolation boundary between guests on the same host. The other attacks target customer authentication, application code or social engineering, not the multi-tenant boundary.

questions.question: A company runs a regulated workload that must not share physical hosts with other tenants. Which option BEST meets this requirement?
options: Dedicated hosts or single-tenant instances
Spreading instances across several availability zones
Larger virtual machine sizes on shared hosts
Enabling stricter security group rules
questions.explanation: Dedicated hosts remove co-tenancy at the physical level. Larger sizes still share hardware, zones address availability and security groups filter traffic.

questions.question: A team deploys a container image containing a known critical vulnerability to production because the pipeline has no gate. What control would have PREVENTED this?
options: Image scanning with an admission policy that blocks vulnerable images
Enabling debug logging inside the container
Adding a bastion host in front of the cluster
Running the containers with a higher CPU quota
questions.explanation: Scanning and enforcing policy at admission stops vulnerable images before they run. Quotas, bastion hosts and logging do not assess image content.

questions.question: An engineer needs to reduce lateral movement between application tiers inside one virtual network after an incident. What is the MOST effective design change?
options: Relying on the perimeter firewall to detect internal movement
Micro-segmentation with deny-by-default rules between workloads
Opening all ports between tiers to simplify troubleshooting during the incident
Moving all tiers into a single flat subnet for simplicity
questions.explanation: Segmentation limits what a compromised host can reach. A flat network and open ports increase movement, and a perimeter device cannot see east-west traffic it never receives.

questions.question: A serverless function that resizes images was given an access role allowing it to read every storage bucket in the account. What is the MOST appropriate action?
options: Increase the function timeout to reduce errors
Keep the existing role but add detailed logging and alerts for all function invocations and errors
Move the function to a larger memory configuration
Replace the role with least-privilege permissions for the one bucket and actions needed
questions.explanation: Over-privileged execution roles are the main serverless risk; fix by least privilege. Logging detects but does not reduce blast radius and timeouts or memory are unrelated.

questions.question: Remote contractors need access to one internal web application only. Which approach BEST follows zero trust principles?
options: A full-tunnel VPN placing contractors on the corporate network
Sharing a common account protected by a long password
Zero trust network access granting per-application sessions after verifying device
Whitelisting the contractors' home IP addresses permanently on the application firewall
questions.explanation: ZTNA grants access to one application per verified session. A VPN gives broad network reach, a shared account destroys accountability and static IP addresses are unreliable and over-broad.

questions.question: Which statement about security groups and network ACLs in a virtual private cloud is MOST accurate?
options: Both are stateless and applied only to internet gateways
Security groups are stateful and instance-level; network ACLs are stateless and subnet-level
Network ACLs are stateful and attached to instances, while security groups are stateless and apply at subnet boundaries
Both are stateful and applied only at the instance level
questions.explanation: Security groups track connections so return traffic is allowed automatically; ACLs evaluate each packet independently and need rules for both directions.

questions.question: An organization finds that identical servers have drifted apart through manual hotfixes, making incidents hard to investigate. Which approach BEST addresses the root cause?
options: Increasing the retention of server logs
Granting all engineers administrator access to fix problems faster
Turning off automatic updates for all hosts
Immutable infrastructure built from versioned images and templates
questions.explanation: Replacing rather than modifying servers removes drift and provides known-good state. Broad admin rights make drift worse, logs do not prevent it and disabling updates adds vulnerability.

questions.question: A dedicated private link connects an on-premises network to a cloud provider. The data classification requires confidentiality in transit. Which statement is MOST accurate?
options: Traffic on private links can be read by any other tenant
Private links encrypt all traffic automatically at line rate with provider-managed keys
Private links remove the need for any access control
The link is private, but encryption must still be configured to meet the requirement
questions.explanation: Private does not mean encrypted; layer encryption on top when required. Other tenants cannot read the traffic, but access controls are still needed.

questions.question: A security team reviews an infrastructure-as-code pipeline. Which control is MOST valuable for preventing misconfigured resources from reaching production?
options: Longer log retention for the deployment tool
A larger approval chain for budget changes
Manual review of resources by an engineer after they have been created
Automated policy-as-code scanning of templates before deployment
questions.explanation: Pre-deployment scanning catches misconfiguration at low cost and is repeatable. After-the-fact review lets exposure occur first, and log retention or budget approval do not check security settings.

questions.question: An attacker obtains the credentials of a cloud administrator who has no multi-factor authentication. Why is this scenario especially severe?
options: The attacker can physically access the provider's data center
The attacker gains direct control of the provider's hypervisors and host firmware
The management plane lets the attacker create, change and delete resources
The attacker can read other customers' data directly
questions.explanation: Management-plane access grants control over the customer's whole environment, which is why strong authentication is essential. Physical access, other tenants' data and hypervisor control are provider-side and not granted by customer credentials.

questions.question: A customer asks how to confirm a provider's data center has redundant power and cooling since it cannot visit. What is the MOST appropriate source of evidence?
options: A network scan of the provider's public addresses
Independent audit reports and certifications covering the facility
A marketing page describing the provider's data centers
The provider's verbal assurance given by a senior executive during a sales call
questions.explanation: Independent reports are the dependable evidence. Marketing and verbal claims are unverified and scanning the provider's addresses is unauthorized and does not assess facilities.

questions.question: Which TWO measures best reduce the risk of an exposed Kubernetes control plane? (Choose two.)
options: Run all workloads with cluster-administrator permissions
Apply least-privilege role-based access control to users and service accounts
Restrict API server access to private networks and authenticated users
Disable audit logging to improve performance
Expose the dashboard publicly for convenience
questions.explanation: Network restriction and least privilege shrink exposure and blast radius. The other options are common causes of cluster compromise.

questions.question: Which TWO are typical security concerns specific to container platforms? (Choose two.)
options: Shared host kernel across containers
Guest operating systems that need separate licenses per container
Vulnerable or untrusted base images
Hypervisor firmware updates on the customer side
questions.explanation: Containers share a kernel and inherit risk from images. They do not carry their own guest operating systems, and hypervisor firmware is the provider's concern.

questions.question: Which THREE actions help protect the cloud management plane? (Choose three.)
options: Disable alerts on console sign-ins from new locations
Share one root account among administrators
Use just-in-time privileged access with approval
Send management API activity to a protected audit log
Require multi-factor authentication for all privileged users
questions.explanation: Strong authentication, time-bound privilege and tamper-resistant logging reduce risk and support investigation. Shared root accounts remove accountability and disabled alerts blind the team.

questions.question: Containers provide stronger isolation than virtual machines because they carry fewer components.
questions.explanation: Containers share the host kernel, so their isolation boundary is weaker than a VM's hypervisor-enforced boundary.

questions.question: In serverless, the customer is responsible for patching the underlying operating system of the function host.
questions.explanation: The provider manages the runtime host; the customer secures code, dependencies, permissions and configuration.

questions.question: Network access control lists are stateless, so rules must allow both inbound and the matching outbound traffic.
questions.explanation: ACLs evaluate each packet independently, unlike stateful security groups.

questions.question: A Type 2 hypervisor is the usual foundation of public cloud platforms.
questions.explanation: Public clouds run Type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisors for performance and a smaller attack surface.

questions.question: A cloud access role that grants a function broad read access across the account is acceptable if the function code is trusted.
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits the damage from bugs, vulnerable dependencies or injection even in trusted code.

questions.question: A BIA shows an order system can be offline for at most two hours and can lose at most ten minutes of transactions. Which pair of objectives does this describe?
options: RTO of two hours and RPO of ten minutes
RTO of ten minutes and RPO of two hours
Maximum tolerable downtime of ten minutes with an RPO of two hours
RTO and RPO both of two hours
questions.explanation: RTO measures time to restore service and RPO measures tolerable data loss in time. The other pairings reverse or conflate them.

questions.question: A company has an RTO of four hours and an RPO of 24 hours for an internal reporting tool and wants the lowest-cost recovery option. Which strategy fits?
options: Warm standby with continuous replication
Backup and restore with nightly backups
Active-active deployment across two regions
Synchronous replication to a hot standby
questions.explanation: The relaxed targets are met by daily backups and manual rebuild. The other options meet far stricter objectives at much higher cost.

questions.question: A bank needs near-zero data loss and failover in seconds for a payment platform, while accepting higher cost. Which design is MOST appropriate?
options: A single zone with a larger instance type
Weekly backups to cold storage
Active-active deployment across availability zones with synchronous replication
Pilot light with asynchronous replication
questions.explanation: Only active-active with synchronous replication supports near-zero RPO and fast failover. Backups and pilot light have longer recovery, and a single zone is a single failure domain.

questions.question: A planner proposes selecting a disaster recovery technology before the business impact analysis is complete. What is the BEST response?
options: Copy the targets from another organization
Proceed with the technology choice, since the available technology determines the recovery objectives
Complete the BIA first, because recovery objectives come from business criticality
Choose the most expensive option to be safe
questions.explanation: The BIA identifies what matters and how fast it must recover; technology choices follow. Cost-driven or borrowed targets are not tied to this organization's impact.

questions.question: A ransomware attack encrypted production data and the backup repository because both shared the same administrator credentials. Which control would have MOST reduced the impact?
options: More frequent full backups written to the same repository with the same credentials
Longer password expiry for administrators
Immutable backups stored separately from production credentials
Larger storage capacity for the repository
questions.explanation: Immutable, logically separated backups survive credential compromise. Backing up more often to the same repository does not protect it, and password policy or capacity does not stop deletion.

questions.question: A cloud application runs in a single availability zone. Which failure scenario is it MOST exposed to?
options: A transient network error
An expired application certificate
Loss of the entire availability zone
Loss of a single virtual machine instance
questions.explanation: Using one zone makes that facility a single point of failure. Individual instance loss could be handled by auto-scaling inside the zone and the others are unrelated to zone design.

questions.question: A multi-region design must comply with a rule that customer data stays within one country. What is the BEST approach?
options: Replicate to whichever region worldwide offers the cheapest storage and compute
Let the provider choose any region dynamically
Disable replication entirely
Choose recovery regions inside the permitted jurisdiction and verify replication
questions.explanation: Resilience must respect residency rules, so recovery sites must be within the jurisdiction. Replicating anywhere violates the rule, no replication sacrifices availability and dynamic placement removes control.

questions.question: Which statement about testing a disaster recovery plan is MOST accurate?
options: A yearly review of the document is sufficient
A backup job that completes without error proves recovery will work
Testing is unnecessary for cloud workloads because the provider handles it
Only a restore or failover test shows whether the objectives can actually be met
questions.explanation: Successful backups say nothing about restore success or timing. Document review does not test procedures, and the customer remains responsible for its own recovery.

questions.question: Which TWO statements correctly relate recovery objectives to design? (Choose two.)
options: RTO should always be set longer than the maximum tolerable downtime
A lower RTO requires more automation and standby capacity
A lower RTO can be met with weekly backups
RPO measures how long restoration takes
A lower RPO requires more frequent replication or backup
questions.explanation: Tighter targets cost more. RPO measures data loss, not restoration time, and the RTO must fit within maximum tolerable downtime.

questions.question: Which TWO risks are specifically associated with cloud adoption as seen in a cloud risk analysis? (Choose two.)
options: Elimination of the need for patching customer-owned systems
Loss of governance and visibility over provider-operated layers
Guaranteed protection from regulatory penalties
Failure of isolation between tenants
questions.explanation: Reduced control and shared-infrastructure isolation are core cloud-specific risks. Customer systems still need patching and regulatory duties remain.

questions.question: The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable time to restore a service after an outage.
questions.explanation: That is the RTO. RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time.

questions.question: Spreading workloads across availability zones protects against the failure of one data-center facility in a region.
questions.explanation: Zones are isolated failure domains within a region.

questions.question: Asynchronous replication guarantees zero data loss during a site failure.
questions.explanation: Asynchronous replication can lose the most recent writes that had not yet been copied.

questions.question: Recovery objectives for a system should be derived from the business impact analysis.
questions.explanation: The BIA ties recovery targets to business harm over time.

questions.question: A team discovers an authorization design flaw one week before launch that requires reworking the data model. In which activity would this flaw MOST cost-effectively have been found?
options: A yearly security awareness course
Threat modeling during design
Penetration testing after deployment
Production monitoring after launch
questions.explanation: Threat modeling at design time finds structural flaws when they are cheapest to fix. Testing after deployment and monitoring find them late, and awareness training does not review a design.

questions.question: A threat model shows that an attacker could send a request pretending to be another user to reach private records. Which STRIDE category does this describe?
options: Spoofing
Denial of service
Tampering
Repudiation
questions.explanation: Impersonating an identity is spoofing. Tampering alters data, repudiation denies actions without evidence and denial of service degrades availability.

questions.question: A company needs to find vulnerable open-source libraries and the exact versions in each release so it can respond quickly to a new advisory. Which approach BEST achieves this?
options: A web application firewall in front of the application
Static analysis of only the company's own source code before each release
Software composition analysis with a maintained software bill of materials
A quarterly code review by a senior developer
questions.explanation: SCA and an SBOM inventory third-party components. SAST of in-house code misses libraries, a WAF is a runtime filter and manual reviews cannot track dependency versions at scale.

questions.question: Which testing technique can find a misconfigured response header and an exploitable input path in a running staging environment WITHOUT access to the source code?
options: Peer code review
Software composition analysis
Static application security testing of the source code
Dynamic application security testing
questions.explanation: DAST probes the running application from outside. SAST and review need source, and SCA examines components rather than behavior.

questions.question: An API returns another customer's invoice when a user changes the invoice number in the request, though authentication succeeded. Which problem is this?
options: Missing rate limiting
Weak transport encryption
Broken object-level authorization
Insufficient logging and monitoring of API activity
questions.explanation: Authentication proved who the caller is, but the API failed to check whether they may access that object. This is the leading API risk. Logging, encryption and rate limiting are separate gaps.
questions.whyTested: Authentication versus authorization failures appear in many forms.

questions.question: A company's build server was compromised and attackers inserted a backdoor into released software, even though the source repository was clean. Which control would have MOST helped detect or prevent this?
options: A WAF rule update for the production site
Encrypting the source repository at rest
Signed build artifacts with provenance verification before deployment
More frequent manual testing of the final application before release
questions.explanation: Provenance and signing show that an artifact came from the trusted pipeline and was not altered. Manual testing may miss a backdoor, a WAF does not examine build integrity and encrypting a clean repository does nothing for the build system.

questions.question: A customer support chatbot built on a large language model retrieves web pages to answer questions. A page contains hidden text telling the model to email customer records to an outside address. Which defense is MOST effective?
options: Increase the model's temperature setting
Move the chatbot to a larger instance size
Add the instruction 'ignore malicious text' to the system prompt as the only control
Treat retrieved content as untrusted and limit the model's tool permissions
questions.explanation: Indirect prompt injection is mitigated by least privilege on tools, output controls and treating inputs as untrusted. A system prompt instruction alone can be overridden, and temperature or instance size are unrelated.
questions.whyTested: The revised outline adds AI application threats such as prompt injection.

questions.question: Which statement about a web application firewall is MOST accurate?
options: It encrypts data stored in the application database
It removes the need to patch application code because attacks never reach the server
It authenticates users to the application
A compensating control that reduces exposure while the code flaw is fixed
questions.explanation: A WAF filters known attack patterns but does not remove vulnerabilities. It does not provide storage encryption or authentication.

questions.question: A security team wants developers to receive vulnerability feedback in their code editor and pull requests before merging. Which practice BEST supports this?
options: Shift-left automated scanning integrated into the build pipeline
Annual penetration tests by an external firm
Monitoring production logs for exceptions
A security sign-off meeting held by the review board after release
questions.explanation: Automated scanning in the pipeline gives fast feedback early. Annual tests and post-release meetings are too late and log monitoring is detective only.

questions.question: Which action BEST reduces the risk that a query to a deployed machine learning model reveals whether a particular person's record was in its training data?
options: Increase the size of the training data without changing the training process
Limit query rates and output detail, and use privacy-preserving training
Store the model in a bucket with a long, random name
Publish the model weights so researchers can inspect them
questions.explanation: Inference attacks rely on repeated, detailed queries; limiting them and training with privacy protections reduces leakage. Publishing weights makes it easier and obscure names are not access control.

questions.question: A cloud-hosted service is vulnerable to SQL injection. Which fix addresses the ROOT cause?
options: Encrypt the database connection with TLS
Block the attacker's current source IP address
Use parameterized queries and validate input against an allow-list
Increase the size of the database instance to absorb malicious queries
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries stop input from being interpreted as code. Blocking an address is temporary, TLS protects transit and size is unrelated.

questions.question: Which TWO practices strengthen API security? (Choose two.)
options: Validate requests against a defined schema and enforce rate limits
Disable logging to protect user privacy
Use a single shared key embedded in all mobile apps
Rely on obscure URL paths to hide endpoints
Authorize each request against the specific object and action
questions.explanation: Per-request authorization and input and rate controls are core. Obscurity, shared embedded keys and no logging weaken security.

questions.question: Which TWO are valid reasons to combine static and dynamic testing in a pipeline? (Choose two.)
options: Either one alone finds every class of vulnerability
Dynamic testing finds runtime and configuration issues static tools miss
Static analysis can detect flaws in the provider's hypervisor
Static analysis finds code flaws early without a running system
Dynamic testing requires access to the source code
questions.explanation: The techniques are complementary. Neither finds everything, DAST does not need source and SAST examines customer code only.

questions.question: OWASP Top 10 is a certification standard that applications must pass to be considered secure.
questions.explanation: It is an awareness list of common risk categories, not a certifiable standard.

questions.question: Threat modeling is most valuable when performed during design, before code is written.
questions.explanation: Design-time modeling finds structural flaws cheaply.

questions.question: A software bill of materials helps identify which applications contain a newly announced vulnerable library.
questions.explanation: An SBOM inventories components so exposure can be assessed quickly.

questions.question: Penetration testing of a cloud provider's shared infrastructure by a customer is allowed without notification.
questions.explanation: Testing must follow the provider's published rules; shared infrastructure is generally off limits.

questions.question: Output from a large language model should be treated as untrusted input by downstream systems.
questions.explanation: Model output can contain injected or incorrect content, so it must be validated like any external input.

questions.question: An organization wants employees to sign in once to access many SaaS applications and have access removed everywhere when they leave. Which approach BEST meets this?
options: A shared password stored in a team document
Federated single sign-on with automated provisioning and deprovisioning
Separate local accounts in each application, managed individually by the application owners
A spreadsheet of accounts reviewed once a year
questions.explanation: Federation centralizes authentication and, with provisioning, makes leaver removal consistent. Shared passwords and separate accounts create orphaned access and spreadsheets are slow and error-prone.

questions.question: A mobile application needs permission to read a user's calendar from a third-party service without ever seeing the user's password. Which protocol is designed for this?
options: OAuth 2.0
SAML assertions for web single sign-on
Basic authentication over TLS
Kerberos ticket granting
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 delegates limited access using tokens. SAML is enterprise web sign-on, basic authentication exposes the password to the app and Kerberos is for enterprise network authentication.

questions.question: A developer states that because their application uses OAuth 2.0 tokens, it already authenticates users. What is the MOST accurate response?
options: OpenID Connect replaces TLS
OAuth handles authorization; OpenID Connect adds the authentication layer
OAuth is purely an authentication protocol
SAML is required for any form of token-based authentication in cloud services
questions.explanation: OAuth was designed for delegated authorization; identity is added by OpenID Connect. The other statements misdescribe the protocols.

questions.question: Cloud administrators hold permanent elevated roles even though they use them only a few times a month. Which change MOST reduces risk?
options: Longer passwords with stricter complexity for administrator accounts
Just-in-time elevation with approval and session recording
Moving administrators to a separate office
Renaming administrator accounts
questions.explanation: Removing standing privilege shrinks the exposure window and adds accountability. Longer passwords help but leave permanent privilege, and the other options do not.

questions.question: A pipeline uses a long-lived access key stored in a repository to deploy infrastructure. Which approach is BEST?
options: Share the key with the whole engineering team
Encode the key in base64 before committing it
Rotate the key once per year but keep it stored in the shared code repository for the team
Use a platform-issued short-lived workload identity with scoped permissions
questions.explanation: Short-lived, scoped credentials issued to the workload remove stored secrets. Yearly rotation leaves a long exposure, sharing widens it and encoding is not protection.

questions.question: A company must grant access based on department, data sensitivity, device compliance and time of day. Which model fits BEST?
options: Attribute-based access control
Role-based access control only
Discretionary access control by file owners
Mandatory access control with fixed labels only
questions.explanation: ABAC evaluates multiple attributes and context at decision time. Role-only models cannot express context, DAC leaves decisions to owners and fixed labels lack contextual factors.

questions.question: Employees use unsanctioned file-sharing services to send work documents. The company wants visibility and policy enforcement over these cloud services. Which tool BEST helps?
options: A hardware security module
A network time server
A cloud access security broker
A load balancer
questions.explanation: A CASB discovers cloud service usage and enforces data and access policy. An HSM stores keys, a time server synchronizes clocks and a load balancer distributes traffic.

questions.question: Which authentication approach is MOST resistant to phishing for a cloud administrator?
options: A long password that is subject to a strict complexity and rotation policy
A security question
A hardware security key or passkey bound to the legitimate site
A one-time code sent by SMS
questions.explanation: Hardware keys and passkeys verify the site and cannot be relayed easily. SMS codes can be intercepted or phished, passwords can be disclosed and questions are guessable.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about federated identity are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: Compromise of the identity provider can affect many connected services
Federation only works inside one organization
The relying service trusts signed assertions from the identity provider
Federation removes the need for authorization decisions
Each service must store a separate copy of the user's password
questions.explanation: Trust is based on signed assertions, and centralization concentrates risk. Services do not store the passwords, authorization is still needed and federation spans organizations.

questions.question: SMS one-time codes are the strongest form of multi-factor authentication available.
questions.explanation: SMS can be intercepted or socially engineered; hardware keys and passkeys are stronger.

questions.question: Separation of duties means one person should not be able to both request and approve a sensitive action.
questions.explanation: Splitting critical tasks prevents any single person from completing fraud or abuse alone.

questions.question: Orphaned accounts of departed employees are reduced by automating provisioning and deprovisioning.
questions.explanation: Automation ties account removal to HR events rather than manual follow-up.

questions.question: A cloud account is suspected to be compromised, but the team finds the management-plane audit trail was never enabled. What is the MOST significant consequence?
options: All data in the account is automatically encrypted
The attacker's activity is automatically blocked
They cannot reliably reconstruct which identities made which changes
The provider will refuse to restore the account until a ticket has been opened
questions.explanation: Management-plane logging records who did what through the console and APIs; without it, reconstruction is guesswork. The other outcomes do not follow from missing logs.

questions.question: During an incident an engineer wants to power off a compromised virtual machine immediately. What should the team do FIRST to preserve evidence while limiting spread?
options: Terminate the instance immediately so the attacker loses access to the host
Delete the instance's logs to avoid confusion
Reboot the instance to clear malicious processes
Isolate the instance and snapshot its disks and memory before it is changed
questions.explanation: Isolation contains spread and snapshots preserve evidence. Terminating or rebooting destroys volatile evidence, and deleting logs destroys what is needed.

questions.question: A team collected disk images from a compromised server but did not record who handled them. What is the MOST significant problem?
options: The broken chain of custody may make the evidence inadmissible
The images cannot be compressed
The images will fail to boot on a standard forensic analysis workstation
The images cannot be hashed
questions.explanation: Chain of custody documents handling and proves integrity. The other concerns are technical details unrelated to admissibility.

questions.question: Which item should be collected FIRST in a live cloud forensic investigation, according to the order of volatility?
options: Printed network diagrams
Archived backup media
Memory contents and running process information
Remote log archives
questions.explanation: Memory is the most volatile and is lost on stop or reboot. Backups and archived logs persist, and diagrams are documentation.

questions.question: A company runs workloads in three cloud providers and each provider's logs use a different format, so analysts miss related alerts. Which action BEST improves detection?
options: Have analysts log in to each provider's console daily
Centralize logs in a SIEM with a normalized schema and consistent identity data
Rely only on each provider's built-in alerts
Disable logging in the two providers whose log formats are the hardest to parse
questions.explanation: Normalization and centralization enable correlation across providers. Manual review does not scale, disabling logs removes visibility and separate alerts miss cross-cloud patterns.

questions.question: An alert shows a developer's credentials were used from two continents within ten minutes. What is the BEST immediate response?
options: Revoke sessions and keys, require MFA again and investigate activity
Change the developer's job title in the directory
Wait for a second alert to confirm the pattern
Reduce log retention to lower storage costs while the investigation proceeds
questions.explanation: Impossible travel indicates likely credential compromise; contain first by revoking access, then investigate. Waiting prolongs exposure and the other options do not address the risk.

questions.question: A security operations lead wants to reduce time to respond for a well-understood, low-risk alert that currently needs manual steps. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Replace the SIEM with a larger one
Require every alert of this type to be escalated to the executive team for approval
Ignore this alert type
Automate the playbook with SOAR and keep analyst approval for high-impact actions
questions.explanation: SOAR automation speeds repeatable steps while keeping humans on risky decisions. A bigger SIEM does not automate response, ignoring alerts removes control and escalating everything overwhelms leadership.

questions.question: Which activity is the cloud customer's responsibility for a virtual machine running in IaaS?
options: Updating the provider's storage firmware
Patching the guest operating system
Maintaining the provider's physical data center
Patching the hypervisor
questions.explanation: In IaaS the customer manages everything above the virtualization layer. The other tasks belong to the provider.

questions.question: A configuration scan shows that several servers no longer match the approved baseline after emergency fixes. Which practice BEST reduces recurrence?
options: Allow all engineers to modify servers directly whenever they judge a change necessary to restore service quickly
Delete the baseline and rely on memory
Detect drift automatically and enforce changes through version-controlled templates
Disable the scans to reduce noise
questions.explanation: Drift detection plus templates keeps configurations governed. Free manual changes create drift and removing the baseline removes the standard.

questions.question: A machine learning model that approves transactions begins behaving differently without any approved update, and recent training data included unreviewed external sources. How should the security team treat this?
options: As a licensing issue for the vendor to resolve
As normal variation that needs no action
As evidence that one of the provider's data centers has suffered a hardware failure
As a potential security incident involving tampering or poisoning, to be investigated
questions.explanation: Unexplained model change can indicate poisoning or tampering. Ignoring it risks fraud, and neither data center failure nor licensing explains it.
questions.whyTested: Model drift as a security incident is called out in the revised outline.

questions.question: Which statement about incident response in the cloud is MOST accurate?
options: The provider alone investigates all incidents on the customer's behalf
Incident response begins when the incident is declared closed
Logs can always be reconstructed after the fact
Preparation, including logging and provider contacts, must be done before an incident because evidence may be ephemeral
questions.explanation: Because resources are ephemeral and access depends on contracts, readiness comes first. The provider does not run the customer's response and logs not collected may be gone.

questions.question: A regulator will be notified of a breach affecting customers. Who should decide the exact content and timing of the external statement?
options: The on-call engineer who found the issue and has the most technical detail
The cloud provider's help desk
The marketing team alone
Legal and compliance leadership with incident command input
questions.explanation: Disclosure carries legal obligations, so legal and compliance lead with technical facts from the response team. Single engineers or marketing lack the authority and providers do not speak for the customer.

questions.question: Which control gives continuous detection of publicly exposed storage and unencrypted databases across many cloud accounts?
options: A tape backup system for archival data
A VPN gateway
A hardware security module
Cloud security posture management
questions.explanation: CSPM continuously evaluates configuration against policy. An HSM, VPN gateway and tape backups do not assess configuration.

questions.question: A team monitors alert counts and reports that more alerts means better security. What is the BEST critique?
options: Fewer logs always mean better security
Metrics should never be reported to leadership because they cause unnecessary concern
Volume does not measure effectiveness; time to detect and respond does
Alert counts are the only valid metric
questions.explanation: Effectiveness is shown by outcomes such as detection and response times. Counts alone may reflect noise, and metrics support leadership oversight.

questions.question: Which TWO actions improve the integrity of logs used for investigations? (Choose two.)
options: Synchronize clocks across systems
Delete old logs weekly to save cost
Allow administrators to edit entries freely
Store logs only on the system that produced them
Forward logs to a central store the source system cannot modify
questions.explanation: Central tamper-resistant storage and consistent time make logs trustworthy. Local-only logs and editable entries can be altered, and weekly deletion destroys evidence.

questions.question: Which TWO are typical challenges of forensics in the cloud? (Choose two.)
options: All evidence is stored on the customer's laptop
Customers always have physical access to the servers
Multi-tenancy never affects evidence handling
Access to underlying hardware and some logs depends on the provider
Ephemeral resources may disappear before evidence is collected
questions.explanation: Short-lived resources and provider-held evidence limit collection. Customers do not have physical access, and multi-tenancy complicates evidence handling.

questions.question: Which THREE are sound preparation activities for cloud incident response? (Choose three.)
options: Wait until an incident to decide who is in charge
Enable and centralize management-plane and workload logging
Agree evidence and escalation procedures with the provider
Set up a pre-approved isolated account for forensic analysis
Disable alerts to reduce noise before audits
questions.explanation: Logging, an isolated analysis environment and agreed provider processes are preparation. Improvising authority and disabling alerts are not.

questions.question: Which TWO inputs belong to threat hunting rather than reactive alert triage? (Choose two.)
options: Closing a ticket generated by a known false positive
A hypothesis that an attacker is abusing a particular cloud role
Applying a vendor patch announced last month
Searching across logs for unusual behavior not tied to any alert
questions.explanation: Hunting is proactive, hypothesis-driven searching. Closing known alerts and patching are routine operations.

questions.question: Terminating a compromised cloud instance is always the best first step because it ends the attacker's access.
questions.explanation: Isolate and capture evidence first; termination destroys volatile data and may lose the instance entirely.

questions.question: A SIEM is only useful if logs from relevant systems are collected and time-synchronized.
questions.explanation: Correlation depends on complete and consistently timed data.

questions.question: Change management applies only to production application code, not infrastructure configuration.
questions.explanation: Infrastructure and configuration changes carry risk and need controlled review and recording as well.

questions.question: The customer is responsible for patching the hypervisor in an IaaS service.
questions.explanation: The provider operates and patches the hypervisor; the customer patches guest systems.

questions.question: A documented chain of custody helps show that digital evidence has not been altered.
questions.explanation: It records every handling step from collection to presentation.

questions.question: Machine learning can assist threat hunting by highlighting anomalous behavior across large volumes of logs.
questions.explanation: ML helps identify patterns humans would miss, though results still need analyst validation.

questions.question: A cloud incident response plan can be developed after an incident because cloud providers keep all logs indefinitely.
questions.explanation: Providers retain logs only to their stated policies; customers must configure and retain their own.

questions.question: Persistent drift between running systems and the approved baseline is a security concern even if the systems work.
questions.explanation: Unreviewed change can open vulnerabilities and complicates investigations.

questions.question: Forensic readiness means collecting evidence only after an incident has been confirmed by the regulator.
questions.explanation: It means preparing logging, tools and agreements in advance so evidence is available when needed.

questions.question: A European retailer uses a cloud provider whose support staff in another country may access personal data. Which mechanism BEST allows this transfer to be lawful if the country lacks an adequacy decision?
options: The provider's marketing assurance of high security
Standard contractual clauses supported by a transfer impact assessment
A statement in the privacy policy that data may be transferred to other countries
Encrypting the data with a key the provider holds
questions.explanation: SCCs with an assessment of destination laws are the standard contract-based safeguard. A policy statement alone is not a lawful mechanism, marketing is not a safeguard and provider-held encryption does not address legal access.

questions.question: A company is the controller of customer data and uses a SaaS processor. A breach occurs at the processor. Which statement is MOST accurate about accountability?
options: Accountability transfers entirely to the processor
No accountability exists for the controller because the processor suffered the breach
The controller remains accountable to regulators and individuals, and the processor must notify the controller
Only the individuals affected are accountable
questions.explanation: Outsourcing processing does not outsource accountability. The processor has duties to notify and assist, but the controller answers to regulators.

questions.question: An auditor asks for evidence that a SaaS provider's security controls operated effectively over the last year. Which report is MOST appropriate?
options: SOC 2 Type I
SOC 2 Type II
A self-published marketing white paper
SOC 3 general-use summary
questions.explanation: Type II tests operating effectiveness over a period. Type I examines design at a point in time, white papers are unverified and SOC 3 is a general summary without detailed testing.

questions.question: A customer wants a comparable public view of a provider's assurance before choosing between two vendors. Which resource is MOST suitable?
options: The CSA STAR registry entries for each provider
The providers' social media accounts
A competitor's sales brochure comparing the two providers
An internal list of preferred vendors
questions.explanation: STAR is a public registry with self-assessments and third-party attestations aligned to the Cloud Controls Matrix. Social media and brochures are unaudited and internal preference lists do not provide evidence.

questions.question: A processor of US health data is hosting records in the cloud. Which contractual document is typically REQUIRED between the covered entity and the provider?
options: A non-compete agreement
A marketing co-branding agreement
A business associate agreement
A software escrow agreement only
questions.explanation: Under HIPAA, providers handling protected health information as business associates must sign such an agreement. The other documents do not satisfy the requirement.

questions.question: A court order requires a company to produce emails stored in a cloud service. Which cloud-specific consideration is MOST important in the eDiscovery plan?
options: The provider's number of employees
The color scheme of the admin console
Whether the provider's marketing website has been redesigned in the last year
Knowing where the data is held, how a legal hold is applied and what the provider will support
questions.explanation: Location, hold mechanisms and provider support determine whether the company can preserve and produce data. The other facts are irrelevant.

questions.question: Management decides to buy cyber insurance to cover part of the financial loss from a major breach. How does this risk treatment BEST classify?
options: Risk acceptance, because no action is taken
Risk transfer, which does not remove accountability or the need for controls
Risk mitigation, because the likelihood of a breach is reduced by the insurer
Risk avoidance, because the risk no longer exists
questions.explanation: Insurance moves part of the financial impact to another party but leaves likelihood and legal accountability. Avoidance means stopping the activity, acceptance means retaining the risk and mitigation reduces likelihood or impact through controls.

questions.question: A department starts using a free file-sharing service to exchange customer data without telling IT. Which response is MOST appropriate?
options: Ignore it because the department owns the data
Discover the usage, assess the risk and offer an approved alternative
Encrypt the service's servers on the department's behalf
Terminate the employees immediately without any review of the business need
questions.explanation: Shadow IT should be discovered, risk-assessed and replaced with a sanctioned option. Ignoring leaves compliance gaps, summary dismissal ignores process and customers cannot encrypt another company's servers.

questions.question: A provider announces a new subprocessor in another jurisdiction. Which customer action is BEST?
options: Review the subprocessor, exercise any right to object and reassess transfers
Cancel the contract without reading the terms
Remove the provider's logo from the website
Accept it automatically because the provider has a strong reputation and certifications
questions.explanation: Contracts and GDPR give customers visibility and a say in subprocessors; review and reassess. Automatic acceptance and cancelling without review do not manage risk.

questions.question: What is the main difference between due diligence and due care?
options: Due care applies only to providers and due diligence only to customers
Due diligence is the response taken after an incident, while due care happens before any incident
They are legal terms with identical meanings
Due diligence is investigating before a decision; due care is acting responsibly to protect assets afterwards
questions.explanation: Diligence is the research performed up front, such as vendor assessment; care is the ongoing practice of protection. They are related but not identical and apply to both parties.

questions.question: A project plans to use customers' behavioral data to train a recommendation model at large scale. Which privacy activity is MOST appropriate before processing begins?
options: Delete all existing consent records before starting the project
Publish the training dataset to the public
Conduct a data protection impact assessment
Wait for a data subject complaint
questions.explanation: Large-scale profiling is the type of high-risk processing for which a DPIA is expected before it starts. The other options increase risk.
questions.whyTested: AI and analytics projects often trigger a DPIA.

questions.question: A US provider receives a legal demand from its government for data stored in a European region belonging to a European customer. Which mitigation BEST limits the provider's ability to hand over readable data?
options: A longer password for the console
Customer-held keys so the provider cannot decrypt the data
A larger service level agreement credit if the provider discloses data
Moving the account to a cheaper pricing tier
questions.explanation: If the provider lacks the key, it cannot produce readable content. SLA credits, pricing tiers and passwords do not affect legal access.

questions.question: Which TWO items should be in a cloud service contract to protect the customer on exit? (Choose two.)
options: A clause preventing the customer from ever changing provider
A provider right to keep copies for its own analytics
Data return in a usable format within a defined period
Silence on data ownership
Verified deletion of remaining copies including backups
questions.explanation: Return and verified deletion support reversibility. Lock-in clauses, provider retention for its own use and ambiguity work against the customer.

questions.question: Which TWO are reasons customers rely on third-party audit reports for cloud providers? (Choose two.)
options: Reports are produced by the customer itself
Reports remove the customer's compliance duties
Direct customer audits of large multi-tenant providers are usually impractical
Independent reports give comparable evidence of control design and operation
Providers are legally forbidden from being audited
questions.explanation: Scale and multi-tenancy make direct audits impractical, and independent reports give assurance. Providers can be audited, customers retain obligations and independence means the reports are not self-produced.

questions.question: Which TWO risk treatments reduce the likelihood or impact of a risk through action rather than shifting or retaining it? (Choose two.)
options: Moving the risk to the provider by contract alone
Stopping the risky activity altogether
Documenting acceptance by the business owner
Buying insurance
Implementing additional security controls
questions.explanation: Mitigation reduces the risk and avoidance removes the activity. Insurance and contracts transfer and documented acceptance retains it.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about GDPR are accurate? (Choose two.)
options: It applies only to companies headquartered in the EU
It forbids any transfer of personal data outside the EU
It can apply to a non-EU company processing personal data of people in the EU
It exempts companies that use cloud providers
A processor must handle personal data only on the controller's documented instructions
questions.explanation: GDPR has extraterritorial reach and binds processors by controller instructions. It is not limited to EU headquarters, has no cloud exemption and permits transfers under lawful mechanisms.

questions.question: A SOC 2 Type I report describes how controls operated effectively over a period of months.
questions.explanation: Type I covers design at a point in time; Type II covers operating effectiveness over a period.

questions.question: Moving to the cloud transfers accountability for compliance from the customer to the provider.
questions.explanation: The customer remains accountable even where the provider performs some controls.

questions.question: ISO/IEC 27018 provides guidance on protecting personal data in public clouds.
questions.explanation: It addresses providers acting as processors of personally identifiable information.

questions.question: Under GDPR a controller must notify the supervisory authority of a reportable breach within 72 hours of becoming aware.
questions.explanation: This is the statutory deadline unless the breach is unlikely to result in risk to individuals.

questions.question: A legal hold overrides normal retention schedules for relevant data.
questions.explanation: Deletion of potentially relevant data must be suspended until counsel releases the hold.

questions.question: CSA STAR Level 1 is a third-party certification performed by an independent auditor.
questions.explanation: Level 1 is a self-assessment; third-party audit or certification is Level 2.

questions.question: Risk acceptance should be decided and documented by the business owner of the affected asset.
questions.explanation: Security advises, but the owner with authority over the business impact accepts residual risk.

questions.question: Pseudonymized personal data is outside the scope of GDPR.
questions.explanation: Because the data can be re-identified with additional information, it remains personal data.

questions.question: Data residency and data sovereignty refer to exactly the same concept.
questions.explanation: Residency is where data is stored; sovereignty concerns which country's laws govern it.

lessons.title: Cloud Foundations and Shared Responsibility
lessons.summary: What makes something cloud, the service and deployment models, who is responsible for what, and the emerging technologies (AI, confidential computing) the newer outline folds in.
lessons.reading:
Cloud computing is a way of renting computing power instead of owning it. The formal definition used by the exam, from NIST, names five essential characteristics: on-demand self-service (you provision resources yourself, without filing a ticket), broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity and measured service. If a vendor hosts a server for you but you must phone them to resize it and pay a flat monthly fee, that is hosting, not cloud. The characteristic that most shapes security is resource pooling, because it produces multi-tenancy: many customers sharing the same physical machines, separated only by software. Isolation between tenants is therefore a cornerstone of cloud security and a favorite exam topic.

Cloud services come in three service models that differ in how much of the technology stack the provider runs for you. In infrastructure as a service you get virtual machines, storage and networks and manage everything from the guest operating system upward. In platform as a service the provider also runs the operating system and runtime, and you bring only your application and data. In software as a service you simply use a finished application. As you move from infrastructure to software, the provider takes over more of the stack and you give up control. That trade is the heart of the shared responsibility model: the provider secures the cloud itself (facilities, hardware, hypervisor, core services) and the customer secures what they put in the cloud and how they configure it. The line moves with the service model, but a few things never move. Data, identities and access decisions, and the choice of settings are always the customer's, and accountability to regulators cannot be handed to anyone.

Deployment models describe who owns and shares the environment. A public cloud is open to many customers. A private cloud serves one organization. A hybrid cloud binds two different models together so workloads and data can move between them, and a community cloud is shared by organizations with a common concern, such as the same regulator. Multi-cloud is a different idea altogether: using more than one provider.

Architects also weigh vendor lock-in. Portability, interoperability and reversibility are the properties that keep an exit possible, and the ISO/IEC 17789 cross-cutting aspects (auditability, availability, governance, privacy, regulatory, resiliency, security, service levels and more) act as a checklist of things to consider before adopting any service.

The outline also asks how newer technologies change the picture. Artificial intelligence and machine learning make training data, models and prompts into assets to classify and protect, and the customer keeps responsibility for them even on a fully managed service. Confidential computing protects data in use by running code inside a hardware-based trusted execution environment. Quantum computing threatens today's public-key algorithms, which is why architects favor crypto agility. Underlying all of this are three design principles to reach for in almost any scenario: defense in depth, least privilege and zero trust, in which identity rather than network location decides who gets in.
lessons.fundamentalsLabel: New to cloud security? See the everyday analogy
lessons.fundamentals: Think of renting an apartment in a large building. The landlord looks after the structure, the locks on the front door, the elevators and the fire alarms; you decide who gets a key to your flat and what you keep inside. If you leave your door unlocked, the landlord's excellent building security does not help you. The more furnished and serviced the apartment (the move from bare unit to hotel suite), the more the landlord handles, but you never hand over the question of who you let in or what you store. Other tenants share the walls and the plumbing, which is multi-tenancy, so the quality of the soundproofing between units matters. That is the shared responsibility model and the reason isolation is always on the exam.
commonTraps: Hybrid cloud binds different deployment models together; using two public providers is multi-cloud, and the exam deliberately blurs the two.
Moving up the stack toward SaaS shifts operating duties to the provider but never shifts accountability for data, identities or compliance.
A brokered or resold service is still your accountability: a cloud service broker adds value but does not take on your legal duties.
Elasticity means automatic scaling in both directions; a manual upgrade to a bigger instance is only scalability.
Encryption in transit and at rest do not protect data in use; confidential computing is the answer when the stem asks about processing.
lessons.scenario: A retailer migrates its order system from a managed hosting contract to a public cloud and a handful of software-as-a-service tools. The CIO assumes security is now the provider's job and cancels the quarterly access review. Six months later a former contractor's account, still active in a SaaS tool, is used to download customer lists. The provider's platform was never breached; the failure sat on the customer's side of the line, which is exactly where the model says identity and data decisions live.
lessons.onTheJob: Start every cloud project by building a responsibility matrix for the specific services you intend to use, because the split differs by service and even by feature. Most providers publish one, but translate it into named owners and controls on your side. Keep an exit plan alive: know where your data would go, in what format, and how long it would take. And treat identity as your perimeter: most real-world cloud compromises begin with a stolen credential or an overly permissive role, not with a defeat of the provider's hypervisor.

lessons.title: Data Lifecycle, Classification and Loss Prevention
lessons.summary: Where data lives, how it is classified and handled across the life cycle, and the controls that stop it leaking: discovery, DLP, IRM, masking and secure deletion.
lessons.reading:
Data security begins with a simple question that many organizations cannot answer: what data do we have and where is it? The cloud data life cycle gives a structure for the answer. Data is created, stored, used, shared, archived and finally destroyed, and a different control matters most at each stage. At creation you classify the data and assign an owner. While stored it needs encryption and access control. While used it needs monitoring and rights management. When shared, it needs protection that follows it. At the end it needs retention rules, legal holds respected and verified destruction.

Classification is the keystone. It means labeling data by sensitivity and business impact, for example public, internal, confidential and restricted, so that handling rules follow from the label. The data owner, a person in the business who is accountable for the data, decides the classification; custodians such as the IT team and the cloud provider apply the controls. Before you can classify, you must discover: scanning storage, databases and files for sensitive content using patterns, labels and increasingly machine learning.

Once data is found and labeled, two families of control keep it in bounds. Data loss prevention watches data as it moves and blocks policy violations, such as card numbers leaving through a personal cloud account. Information rights management, by contrast, attaches protection to the file itself so that it can be opened only by permitted people and can be revoked after sharing. The difference matters on the exam: if the stem asks how to retain control after a document has left your environment, think IRM; if it asks how to stop sensitive content leaving, think DLP.

Not all copies of data need the real values. Masking replaces sensitive fields with realistic fake ones, which is ideal for test environments. Anonymization removes the link to a person irreversibly, so the data is no longer personal data; pseudonymization replaces identifiers but keeps a way back, so privacy law still applies. Tokenization, covered in the next lesson, swaps values for random tokens that point at a vault.

Retention and destruction deserve respect because they are where cloud differs most. Keep data too long and you enlarge breach and discovery exposure; delete too early and you violate regulations or a legal hold, which suspends normal deletion when litigation is likely. In the cloud you cannot degauss or shred the provider's disks, so the accepted answer for guaranteeing deletion is cryptographic erasure: encrypt the data with keys you control and destroy every copy of the key.

Finally, the newer outline adds data lakes and training datasets to the picture. A large central repository of mixed data needs fine-grained access control and lineage records, and a dataset used to train models needs integrity protection too, because a poisoned input quietly corrupts every model built from it. Always map data flows so you know which regions, providers and sub-processors touch the data, since privacy law attaches to those paths.
lessons.fundamentalsLabel: New to data security? See the everyday analogy
lessons.fundamentals: Picture the paper records of a large hospital. Someone has to decide which files are routine and which are highly sensitive, and mark them accordingly; that is classification. Staff walk through the building to find forgotten files in corridors and cupboards; that is discovery. Guards at the exit check bags for stray patient files; that is data loss prevention. A special folder that, once handed to another clinic, can still be locked remotely by the hospital is rights management. Old records follow a schedule for how long they must be kept and are then shredded, unless a lawyer places a hold on them. In the cloud you cannot watch the shredder, so you lock the records in a safe and destroy the only key.
commonTraps: Discovery comes before classification, and classification comes before DLP rules and encryption choices: the exam punishes answers that skip ahead.
Pseudonymized data is still personal data under privacy law; only effective anonymization takes it out of scope.
IRM travels with the file and can be revoked; DLP only governs egress, so it cannot reclaim a document that already left.
Logical deletion or a console delete does not prove physical erasure in a shared platform; cryptographic erasure is the standard answer.
A legal hold overrides retention schedules and auto-delete rules, even when storage cost or policy says delete.
lessons.scenario: A healthcare analytics company copies production patient records into a test environment for a developer. A bucket in the test account is accidentally made public and the records are exposed. The team had neither discovered where copies of the data lived nor masked non-production copies.
